property_statement: Raft log-matching / state-machine safety under crash recovery: a leader may only count a follower as matched for a log index when the follower's log shares the leader's committed prefix, so that every committed index is durably replicated with identical (index,term,payload) entries on a quorum; consequently, replicas must never apply different command payloads at the same log index, and a follower that acknowledges an append must have truncated any pre-existing conflicting entries above its committed index.
summary: raftLog.maybeAppend drops the first entry of an incoming MsgApp batch from its conflict scan whenever that entry is an empty (leader no-op) entry located exactly at the follower's current lastIndex and is followed by a non-empty entry, without verifying the term of the entry already occupying that index on the follower. A follower that carries an uncommitted divergent payload entry (older term) at that exact index therefore keeps the divergent entry, appends the leader's later entries after it, and acks `lastnewi` for a log it does not share with the leader. The leader then counts that ack toward the commit quorum and can commit a prefix whose copies differ across the quorum members, so the divergent payload can be applied at the committed index on the follower while other replicas apply the empty no-op, breaking Log Matching. Reachability requires the follower's divergent tail to be a single uncommitted entry at the new leader's first no-op index and requires the leader's initial no-op-only probe to be delayed/reordered behind the combined no-op+proposal batch; these are message-ordering conditions within the fault model but were not established by execution.

source_evidence.claim: maybeAppend first matches a.prev, then computes lastnewi over the whole batch, then removes check[0] from conflict scanning when check[0].Index == l.lastIndex(), check[0].Data is empty, and check[1].Data is non-empty, without ever comparing the follower's term at check[0].Index with the incoming entry's term. The remaining entries are scanned by findConflict, any conflict below committed panics, and otherwise only a.entries[ci-offset:] is appended; finally commitTo(min(committed,lastnewi)). So a divergent existing tail entry at lastIndex that differs only in term is neither detected nor truncated when the skip fires.

findConflict defines conflict as same index but different term (matchTerm failure) and returns the first conflicting index; entries beyond the follower's lastIndex also fail matchTerm and are reported as the first new index. This is the term check that the empty-entry skip in maybeAppend bypasses for check[0].

truncateAndAppend only discards existing unstable entries when fromIndex is at or below the current region; when entries are appended from an index that equals offset+len(entries) (follower already at that tail) or from an index equal to offset, the pre-existing entry X is retained and the new entries are appended after/at it, so a divergent tail entry survives when maybeAppend does not truncate it.

becomeLeader appends an empty no-op entry at r.raftLog.lastIndex()+1 as the leader's first term entry, after reset() which has set every follower's Next to the pre-no-op lastIndex+1. This makes the no-op the first entry of the first non-empty batch a follower may receive from the new leader.

On a MsgProp, stepLeader appends the proposed entries (which follow the no-op in the same term) and then calls bcastAppend, which can transmit the no-op and the proposal together in a single MsgApp batch from the follower's Next.

maybeSendAppend sends a MsgApp whose Index/LogTerm is pr.Next-1 and whose Entries start at pr.Next; a probe-state follower with Next equal to the no-op index therefore receives prev=(k-1) with entries [no-op@k, proposal@k+1,...] as one batch, exactly matching the skip precondition of maybeAppend.

On a non-reject MsgAppResp, stepLeader calls pr.MaybeUpdate(m.Index) and then r.maybeCommit(); maybeCommit commits r.trk.Committed() (majority of pr.Match acks) when the entry at that index has the leader's term, trusting the follower's ack index without any verification that the follower's log prefix matches the leader's.

CommittedIndex returns the quorum-th smallest acked Match value across voters, so a follower's spurious ack of lastnewi (over a divergent prefix) is directly incorporated into the leader's commit index computation.

mechanism.violated_obligation: Before a leader counts a follower's MsgAppResp ack toward the commit quorum, the follower must have truncated every pre-existing entry that conflicts (same index, different term or payload) with the replicated batch, so any follower in the commit quorum stores a log that is an exact prefix of the leader's committed log. The code discharges this obligation in raftLog.findConflict via per-entry term matching, but the empty-entry fast path in raftLog.maybeAppend (log.go:116-121) exempts the first batch entry from that term check whenever it is a payload-free no-op located at the follower's lastIndex.
mechanism.decisive_relation: The skip guard `check[0].Index == l.lastIndex() && len(check[0].Data)==0 && len(check[1].Data)>0` drops check[0] from the conflict scan without asserting `l.term(check[0].Index) == check[0].Term`. When the follower's existing entry at that index is an uncommitted payload entry X from an older term (reachable after the prior leader appended X only to this follower and crashed), findConflict is evaluated only on check[1:], reports the first new index above the divergent entry, and only a.entries[1:] is appended; X survives and the follower acks lastnewi = prev.index + len(all entries). The leader then folds that ack into tracker/progress Match and quorum.CommittedIndex, possibly committing the no-op index and the proposal on a quorum {leader, follower} whose durable copies at the no-op index differ (no-op vs X).

causal_chain: Leader O (term t) appends an uncommitted payload entry X at index k and replicates it only to follower F; O crashes; F's log tail at index k holds X (older term) while its prefix through k-1 matches the rest of the cluster.

A new leader L (term t+1, log through k-1) is elected, appends its empty no-op at index k, and receives a proposal appended at k+1; bcastAppend (or the heartbeat-resp retry path) reaches F with a single MsgApp prev=(k-1) carrying [no-op@k(empty), proposal@k+1,...] before F has seen the no-op-only probe.

F runs raftLog.maybeAppend: the skip at log.go:116-121 removes the no-op from findConflict's term check; findConflict sees no conflict below k+1 on the remaining entries; X at index k is retained by unstable.truncateAndAppend; F acks lastnewi >= k+1 for a log whose index k differs from L's.

L counts F's ack via pr.MaybeUpdate and commits the proposal index (implicitly committing index k) on quorum {L,F} by maybeCommit/r.trk.Committed() without any prefix verification, and propagates Commit >= k to F.

F advances committed to >= k and applies X at index k while L and other replicas apply the empty no-op at k; if F or L crashes before any later probe overwrites X on F, the committed region is durably stored with two different payloads on the quorum that committed it, and restarting replicas can apply distinct values at the same index, violating Log Matching / state-machine safety.

test_sketch.precondition: P: 3-node fixed voter set {L,G,H} plus follower F (partitionable), initial committed log through index k-1. Crash/restart sequence: leader O in term t appends entry X at index k and replicates only to F, then crashes before commit (F holds durable/unstable X@k, lastIndex=k, committed=k-1). L is elected in term t+1 by {L,G,H} with log through k-1 and becomes leader (appending empty no-op at k).
actions: A1: Block/drop the no-op-only MsgApp that L's stepCandidate/becomeLeader bcastAppend sends to F, and deliver L's later combined MsgApp (prev=k-1, entries [no-op@k empty, proposal@k+1 with payload 'P']) to F first (message reorder/delay/drop under the fault model).

A2: F processes the combined batch through handleAppendEntries/maybeAppend, retains X@k, appends k+1, and acks lastnewi=k+1; L (plus F) forms the commit quorum and commits index k+1; L broadcasts Commit=k+1; F applies committed entries including X at index k; then F crashes and restarts from durable state, or L crashes to fix the committed region as X-vs-no-op copies.
test_sketch.violation: V: F applies payload X at index k (or a restarted replica derived from F's durable log serves X at index k) while L/G/H apply the empty no-op at the same index k, i.e. two distinct entry payloads are committed/applied at one log index, and the follower that supplied the commit quorum ack did not share the leader's log prefix at index k.
test_sketch.oracle: O: Compare per-node applied logs/state-machine results after stabilization: entry at index k differs in payload (X vs empty no-op) between F and {L,G,H}, or after L+F crash and restart the two recovered logs disagree at index k while both report index k as committed.

uncertainties: Reachability requires F's divergent uncommitted tail to be exactly one payload entry whose index equals the index of the new leader's first no-op, with F's prefix through k-1 matching the leader's log; other tail lengths self-heal through normal per-entry conflict truncation.

The scenario requires the leader's initial no-op-only probe MsgApp to be delayed or dropped behind a later combined no-op+proposal batch so that F's first processed batch from L triggers the skip; whether the rafttest/network harness can realize this exact reordering was not established (no execution available).
F must apply the divergent entry X (commit index reaching k) before any delayed no-op-only probe truncates and replaces X; otherwise the divergence self-corrects.

The commit quorum {L,F} must be reachable while G/H are unavailable or not yet caught up, and the durability of X on F before its ack is assumed satisfied per the Ready/async append contract so that the ack is a genuine durable acknowledgment.
